data.one_liner: On‑device hand detection, landmarks and gesture recognition using LiteRT models.
data.what_it_does: The package runs MediaPipe hand detection locally, returning 21‑point 3D landmarks, handedness and a set of predefined gestures. It works on mobile, desktop and web without any remote API.
use_when: You need offline hand tracking on multiple platforms
You require 3D hand landmarks and built‑in gesture classification
You want GPU/NPU acceleration where available
avoid_when: You prefer a pure Dart solution without native OpenCV dependencies
You target very old devices or browsers without WebGPU support
strengths: Cross‑platform: Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, Web
Supports GPU/NPU via LiteRT for better performance
weaknesses: Requires native libraries (opencv_dart, dartcv4) and specific Flutter/Dart versions
Setup can be complex (hooks, iOS deployment target, native linking)
data.setup_notes: Requires Dart 3.10+ and Flutter 3.47.5+. Add hooks user_defines for iOS deployment target (>=15.0). Ensure native dependencies (opencv_dart, dartcv4) are compiled for each platform. Include camera_desktop for desktop camera use. May need to run flutter clean after changes.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a lower‑level TFLite API without the heavy OpenCV and LiteRT stack, suitable for simpler models or when you want full control over inference.

alternatives.name: google_mlkit_commons
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers Google‑backed ML Kit APIs with easier setup on mobile, though it relies on Google services and may not support desktop/web.
